anomalies.description: A large, sustained explosion with intense fireball and expanding smoke plume, occurring near or behind silhouetted high-rise buildings at night. The blast grows in intensity from f0 to f14, peaking around f14–f15 with a massive bright flash that illuminates the scene.

A large, bright explosion erupts with intense fireball and rapidly expanding smoke plume, visible across multiple frames; the initial blast phase peaks around 6.0–7.0 s.; Sustained secondary combustion and possible additional detonations or fuel-fed fire following the initial blast; brightness fluctuates but remains high, with continued fireball and smoke expansion through 11.5 s.

A large, sustained fireball and plume of smoke erupts and persists in the distance, consistent with a major explosion (e.g., industrial or chemical), with visible expansion and bright incandescence across all frames.

A large, sustained explosion with intense fireball, rapidly expanding turbulent fire cloud, and ejection of incandescent debris/sparks upward and outward; the fireball evolves into a mushrooming plume with visible rain-like droplets (likely condensed vapor or water spray) falling through the hot column, indicating a high-energy detonation event.

A large, sustained fireball with violent ejection of incandescent debris and dense smoke, characteristic of a major explosion (e.g., fuel or chemical detonation), evolving over time from a multi-lobed fireball to a rising column of flame and smoke.

A large, rapidly expanding fireball with intense yellow-white core and orange-red plume, accompanied by upward ejection of incandescent debris and dense smoke—consistent with a high-energy explosion (e.g., fuel or chemical detonation) rather than sustained combustion.

A large, sustained fireball with intense yellow-white core and expanding orange-red plume dominates the scene, consistent with a major explosion (e.g., fuel or chemical detonation) occurring at ground level near structures and a crane. The fireball persists and evolves over ~7.5 seconds without diminishing to background fire levels, indicating an initial blast followed by vigorous combustion.

Massive, rapidly expanding fireball with turbulent orange-yellow flames and dense smoke, accompanied by visible ejecta/sparks and structural silhouettes being overwhelmed—consistent with a large-scale explosion (e.g., fuel or chemical detonation) rather than sustained fire alone.

Secondary or continuing explosive phase: bright localized fireball re-ignites or surges near building silhouette (right), with sustained upward ejection of sparks and hot fragments; plume begins to dissipate but remains highly energetic.
